_metadata.description: Sector-to-adversary targeting model. Scores how likely each documented threat actor is to target a given sector, to prioritize which actor(s) to emulate in an intelligence-led test.
_metadata.scoring: relevance_score 1-10: combines sector targeting history, motivation fit, and recent activity. Higher = emulate first.

top_threats.rationale: Direct financial theft is a state revenue stream; SWIFT heists, crypto theft
Payment card and financial system theft is their core business
Help-desk social engineering + ransomware against financial targets
High-volume ransomware; finance is a high-value extortion target
Healthcare is a top ransomware target — high urgency, pays to restore care
Espionage against pharma/health research + opportunistic profit
Vaccine/research espionage (documented COVID-era targeting)
Supply chain compromise of software vendors is a signature move (SolarWinds)
Software supply chain attacks + rapid CVE weaponization
Targets tech/telecom via help-desk social engineering
Fake job offers targeting developers; trojanized dev tools
POS malware and payment card theft is their specialty
Documented intrusions into retail/hospitality
Opportunistic ransomware
Core espionage target set
State espionage against government entities
Ransomware against municipal/state government
Documented energy-sector targeting; destructive capability
Telecom/utility targeting for espionage
Ransomware against manufacturing/utilities

selection_guidance.how_to_use: Pick your sector, take the top 1-3 actors by relevance_score, and build emulation scenarios from their characteristic_ttps in threat-actors.json. Emulate the highest-scoring actor first — it represents your most probable serious adversary.
coverage_strategy: Emulate the #1 actor to test against your MOST LIKELY threat
Add a second actor with a DIFFERENT initial-access style (e.g. one supply-chain, one social-engineering) to broaden detection coverage
Re-run quarterly — actor TTPs and sector targeting shift over time
do_not: Do not emulate an actor irrelevant to your sector just because it's famous
Do not treat the score as attribution — it is a prioritization aid
Do not skip the purple-team replay — emulation without detection tuning wastes the intel
